subject: Localization model discovery — follow-up & sample plan
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Anders <julia.anders@nordictranslate.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Localization model discovery — follow-up & sample plan

Hi Julia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a concrete next-step plan so we keep momentum: 

Call highlights (30 min):
- Primary use case: multi-locale post-edit / initial translation + in-context consistency checks for EU languages (SV/DA/NO/PL) and selective APAC support (TH, VI).
- Volume: ~200k tokens/month to start, expected to grow 3x in 12 months.
- Latency SLO: 300–400ms p50 for short inference flows; batchy offline jobs can be higher.
- Security: data must stay in EU; prospect wants VPC/private deployment conversation later in procurement.

Recommended evaluation plan (proposed, ~2 weeks):
1) Baseline runs: run our 13B and 30B quantized variants on a curated prompt set for the target locales (we'll test redwood-13b-quant and redwood-30b-qf16).
2) Benchmarks: automated pass/fail on locale-specific metrics (BLEU-ish, chrF, and a semantic similarity check using our embedding reranker).
3) Quality regression checks: include a guarded set of 50 examples where previous deploys have failed (Polish diacritics, Thai segmentation).
4) Run human evals (crowd + in-country linguists) for top 3 model-configs.

Shared artifacts: attaching a starter prompt-set and a compact benchmark CSV with expected fields. Also pv link to a Drive folder where we'll push raw outputs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Gq-example-benchmarks

Next steps / asks:
- Julia: please confirm the list of target locales (I used SV, DA, NO, PL, TH, VI) and send any existing glossaries or MT post-edits you want included.
- Procurement: we can share a scoped mutual action plan and an estimated committed cost for Dedicated or Private (per your preference).
- Redwood (Rachel + Priyom): kick off a quick internal run on redwood-13b-quant vs redwood-30b-qf16 using the sample prompts attached; capture token cost and latency distributions.

Attachments (attached): prompt-set-samples-v1.txt, redwood-benchmarks-eu-apac-20270618.csv

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up next week after your confirmation.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0127

Subject: Re: Localization model discovery — follow-up & sample plan

Hi Alex —

Great summary, thanks. Confirming target locales: Swedish (SV), Danish (DA), Norwegian (NO), Polish (PL), Thai (TH), Vietnamese (VI). We also have a small Norwegian Nynorsk slice (approx 5k tokens) — can that be included?

I've attached two files: a short glossary (nordic-glossary-v1.xlsx) and a handful of post-edit examples (nt-postedits-samples.zip). Please note: Polish sample set includes many diacritic-sensitive cases and several legal-phrase constraints ("Avtale" vs "avtaler"). Those are high priority.

Question on models: are the redwood-13b-quant and redwood-30b-qf16 the same base architecture with different quant/tuning, or are they distinct families? Which would you expect to generalize better on low-resource targets like Vietnamese and the Nynorsk slice?

We can do the mutual action plan once we see a short pilot result. Procurement would prefer Private deployment but wants an estimated TCO for a 6-month pilot first.

Julia
Julia Anders
Head of Localization — NordicTranslate Inc.
procurement@nordictranslate.com | +47 21 00 99 00

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Anders <julia.anders@nordictranslate.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Localization model discovery — follow-up & sample plan

Hi Julia —

Thanks for the quick confirmation and the attachments (received). Nynorsk slice is fine — include it in the evaluation set and mark it separately so we can measure degradation vs Bokmål.

To answer your model question briefly: both model configs come from the same family trunk in our catalog but diverge in compilation/quantization and tuning profiles. redwood-13b-quant is lower cost, optimized for throughput with aggressive 8-bit matmul kernels; redwood-30b-qf16 uses an f16-friendly execution path with additional locale-aware fine-tuning we applied for better morphological handling. Expectation: 30b variant will typically outperform on low-resource morphologically-rich languages (Polish, Vietnamese) at higher cost; 13b can be surprisingly strong for Scandinavian languages where domain similarity is high.

What we'll run this week (deliverables by Thu EOD):
- Short pilot: 500 in-context translation pairs across the target locales (includes Nynorsk).
- Benchmarks: redwood-benchmarks-eu-apac-20270618.csv (attached) will be populated with columns: locale, model, prompt_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_p50, latency_p95, chrF, semantic_sim_score.
- Prompt set: prompt-set-samples-v1.txt (attached) — please review and flag any brand/locale constraints.
- Human eval plan link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Gq-example-benchmarks (I'll add the evaluation rubric and rater instructions).

Quality regression guardrails: we have a small "regression set" of 50 golden examples (Polish legal phrases + Thai segmentation) that will immediately fail the run if semantic_sim_score drops below 0.82 — this prevents silent regressions. Priyom, please ensure we include the regression set as the first pass.

Commercials / TCO: we'll produce a 6-month Private deployment estimate (including infra + engineering OPEX) in the mutual action plan PDF; draft attached as mutual-action-plan-NT-DEAL-2467.pdf. Procurement: if you prefer, we can run the pilot on Redwood Hosted (fastest) and then convert to Private for the committed phase. There are tradeoffs; we'll outline them.

Next meeting: are you available Thu 24 Jun 10:00 CEST for a quick results review?

Best,
Alex

Attachments: redwood-benchmarks-eu-apac-20270618.csv (updated), prompt-set-samples-v1.txt, mutual-action-plan-NT-DEAL-2467.pdf

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: NT pilot — immediate action items

Rachel / Priyom — quick internal note summarizing what I need you both to own for the pilot kickoff (so Julia sees coordinated updates).

Action items (priority order):
1) Priyom: run the baseline scripts on redwood-13b-quant and redwood-30b-qf16 against the 500-sample pilot set. Capture latency p50/p95 and token cost. Put raw outputs in the Drive folder and add a short README describing how to reproduce (container + flags). Deadline: Wed 23 Jun EOD PST.
2) Rachel: set up the human eval pipeline for the 3 top model/configs. Book linguists for PL/TH/VI and a small Nordic reviewer pool for SV/DA/NO/Nynorsk. Provide expected per-eval cost and timeline. Deadline: Wed 23 Jun noon PST.
3) Both: flag any "red" regression cases early — the regression set (50 examples) must be run first. If semantic_sim_score < 0.82 for any model, stop and notify me immediately.

Risks / notes:
- Polish diacritics are a known failure mode; if the 13b shows >7% token-level error in diacritic placement we should consider fallback routing to 30b for PL.
- Thai segmentation may require a segmenter pre-pass; if the 30b still underperforms we should include an optional lightweight tokenization step in the pipeline.

I'll send the scheduled invite for Thu 24 Jun 10:00 CEST after Julia confirms. Keep the thread going and paste links to Drive/HuBSpot updates as you have them.

Alex
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
